name: University of California, Santa Barbara
overview:
The University of California, Santa Barbara (UC Santa Barbara or UCSB) is a public land-grant research university in Santa Barbara, California with 23,196 undergraduates and 2,983 graduate students enrolled in 2021-2022. It is part of the University of California 10-university system. Tracing its roots back to 1891 as an independent teachers' college, UCSB joined the University of California system in 1944, and is the third-oldest undergraduate campus in the system, after UC Berkeley and UCLA.


Located on a WWII-era Marine air station, UC Santa Barbara is organized into three undergraduate colleges (College of Letters and Science, College of Engineering, College of Creative Studies) and two graduate schools (Gevirtz Graduate School of Education and Bren School of Environmental Science & Management), offering more than 200 degrees and programs. The university has 10 national research centers, including the Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics and the Center for Control, Dynamical-Systems and Computation. UCSB has various organized research units (ORUs) researching evolutionary psychology, neuroscience, marine science, and more. According to the National Science Foundation, UC Santa Barbara spent $235 million on research and development in fiscal year 2018, ranking it 100th in the nation. UCSB was the No. 3 host on the ARPAnet and was elected to the Association of American Universities in 1995.


Current UCSB faculty includes six Nobel Prize laureates, one Fields Medalist, 39 members of the National Academy of Sciences, 27 members of the National Academy of Engineering, and 34 members of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences. UCSB is classified among "R1: Doctoral Universities – Very high research activity" and is regarded as a Public Ivy. The faculty also includes two Academy and Emmy Award winners, and recipients of a Millennium Technology Prize, an IEEE Medal of Honor, a National Medal of Technology and Innovation and a Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics.
administrative:
1. Application dossier

You will work directly with the partner university regarding your application. All required documents will have to be uploaded on their platform or sent by email before the deadline (see the Americas Teams channel for each application deadline). If you have not received anything yet, it means your nomination has not been sent yet, please be patient.


In the past the partner has asked for the following:

  • Photocopy of passport / Residence permit (valid more than 6 months after return)
  • Registration forms for UCSB (provided once the destination has been validated by the jury)
  • A letter from the bank with a provision of $20,000 dated less than 6 months
  • If the bank letter is from a parent's bank account, it must attest to the relationship and mention that the amount available may be used for your expenses during your year abroad in the United States.
  • Course selection form for UCSB (provided once the destination has been validated by the jury)
  • University insurance subscription consent form (provided once the destination has been validated by the jury)

This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


To be given to Epitech bachelor campus administration to reenroll for the Tech4 (in April/May):

  • The addendum to the contract
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier


2. Visa (more information here)

You can find all the detailed information on the US government website or the Embassy of the US in Paris website. You can check the deadlines for obtaining an appointment here.


1/Admission letter and I-20 form

When you have been admitted to UCSB, you will receive an I-20 form, allowing you to apply for the F-1 student visa at the embassy. Please check the information on I-20 carefully and sign the document.


2/Pay the SEVIS fees

 You must then pay the SEVIS I-901 fees online (here). Make sure you print the receipts. The fees for students are $350.


3/Complete the DS-160 form

Complete DS-160 form and upload an ID photo meeting the following requirements. Print the application form confirmation page to bring to your interview.

You will have to pay a visa application fee (non refundable) before your interview of $185 (more information here).


4/Schedule an appointment at the consulate

For people in France, you need to make an appointment for your interview at the US Consulate. Plan to travel to Paris for it.

If you live in another country, check the different consulate/embassy.


During your interview at the consulate, you must:

  • have the necessary supporting documents to prove that you qualify for the category of visa that you request--document relating to your current studies and its relationship to the studies you wish to pursue in the United States: academic transcript, various certificates, SAT or TOEFL test scores, diplomas, etc.
  • demonstrate, with supporting evidence, to the consular officer that you have solid family, social and financial ties to France and that you intend to return there once your residence permit has expired.
  • prove that you have the financial means necessary to finance your studies and live in good conditions in the United States for the first 12 months. Any document proving your family or relational ties with any person funding your studies, as well as bank statements, tax notices thereof.

Please note that the visa gives you the right to work 20 hours on campus.


3.Insurance and Health

University health insurance

UCSB requires students to purchase the university health insurance, unless your health insurance meets the criteria for a waiver.

You must demonstrate proof of health insurance coverage before arriving to the U.S., as part of your I-20 application.

The insurance brochure summarizing what is covered and not (typically dental and vision are NOT covered and you need to make your own arrangements for these) for 2025 can be found at: student.jcbins.com/1479.

You will first receive an email from the insurance and then you can register so do not try and register before receiving emails from them.

If you have any questions about insurance, please have them contact JCB directly at GGB.JCB.Studentservices@ajg.com


Please also note the following important info: In the US, medical coverage does not usually cover 3rd party liability (it is a separate insurance contract that does), which means the UCSB insurance Anthem is a medical-only insurance.

Coverage is only in the USA but you can also subscribe to a worldwide insurance at: geobluestudents.com


International insurance

In order to be fully covered in the event of an accident (especially outside the region), we recommend that all students take out international insurance during their year abroad. It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information.


In addition, all incoming students must complete a five question Tuberculosis Screening Questionnaire which is located on the Clearances tab in your MyHealth portal. For more information, you can consult the country’s health file at: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/etats-unis


Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.


4. Prepare your arrival

You have the option to take an Airbus from LAX to SB. To book tickets, visit: sbairbus.com The one-way fee per person is approximately $55.

For advice to travelers issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on the host country, click here.
accomodation:
On-campus accommodation (more information here)

They cannot predict nor guarantee that there will be vacancies on campus and the Fall quarter is the one where the probability for international students to get campus housing is the most challenging but this year many international students could secure campus housing. For Winter and Spring quarters there are typically more vacancies.

That said, you can apply for UCSB campus housing as soon as you receive your UCSB NetID which should be by early September 2025 or immediately thereafter. To do so, please visit this link once you have your NetID. 

We should know if there are places left about 2 to 3 weeks before the quarter starts. 

See also this website to see where there might be vacancies


IMPORTANT - For those of you who are interested in applying for campus housing but are only staying for one semester and therefore reluctant to take those contracts on campus (which are are typically for one year), please see below the important information: If students give 30 days or more notice there is a $250 fee to cancel. It increases to $350 if they inform the UCSB Housing in less than 30 days. In the contract there is a clause about it, so depending on the contract they sign, it should indicate the cancellation fee. Put briefly, it would not cost you so much to break/cancel the contract after 3, 6 or even 9 months as this is apparently common practice. 


Off-campus accommodation

International students typically live off campus, usually in privately owned residence halls, homestays, or furnished apartments. Off-campus, non-UCSB housing is available year-round; students make reservations directly with housing providers.  

First, please join the official UCSB WhatsApp group as it will also help you with acaditalicic or housing questions.

Second, the idea is that some of you - when possible at all - may want to take over the lease of those currently in SB who are away for the Fall quarter only. Those staying for the full year may also know of some vacancies so please do not hesitate to post a message asking for help. Finding accommodation at Santa Barbara can also be challenging and requires some research (and resilience) so they are sending informations to recommend the best sites and courses of action for you to start with your research as soon as possible.


1. Facebook groups

Make sure you join the FB groups IV Housing UCSB and UCSB Housing as there are lots of subleasing offers already there for one quarter.


2. Appartment listing websites

  • SBCC (Santa Barbara Community College) Housing list  
  • Student Roomstay - https://studentroomstay.com/abrego 
  • Coral Group - https://www.coralgroupsb.com/ 
  • Roomster - https://www.roomster.com/en-GB/haveshare/santa-barbara-ca-usa 
  • Craiglist Santa Barbara (this is a peer-to-peer website, equivalent to French Le Bon Coin, if you are French). Check their housing section and within that:
  • the room and share section here 
  • the sublets and temporary section here 

You can also look at their sublet/temporary link if you come to SB a little before your program starts for the orientation and for exploring housing options that are not offered online.


There will be different prices for different locations there too so do spend enough time exploring and visit regularly for updates.

  • St George's Associates - https://www.stgeorgeassociates.com/ (for full year singles)
  • The Loop Isla Vista - https://www.theloopiv.com/ 

This person who works at UCSB also typically has a couple of rooms to rent every quarter on a first-come-first-served basis: sofiamuller@ucsb.edu


 Important Notes:

  • Subleasing is a normal practice at UCSB. This is often because UCSB full -time students who leave UCSB to go abroad for one or more quarters will be looking to sublease/rent out their apartments/rooms for the duration of their study abroad and to get their rooms back when they return to Santa Barbara. You will find many of these on the FB groups mentioned above. This is a good way to find your accommodation but there can be scams.
  • If the offers sound too good to be true, be careful. 
  • Always ask the people who propose to sublease to have a video conference on WhatsApp or Telegram so you can see the house and room at the right address.
  • Never pay a deposit before seeing the apartment for yourself.
courses:
Credits

Students must validate 36 credits over the course of the year, or 12 per trimester, to validate 60 ECTS.


Academic Calendar

September - June


Department and Courses

Students will take the International Certificate Program, which allow them to get three certificates:

  • Business Administration
  • Digital Marketing
  • Applied AI


The program takes place over 3 trimesters. Students must take 12 credits per trimester.


Important notes

  • Presence in class is compulsory, under penalty of loss of visa and repatriation to France at the student's expense (impact on credits).
  • The courses are most likely more academic than at EPITECH.
  • The course list is given for information only. It can change from year to year.
  • If a course is not available when you arrive on site, EPITECH cannot be held responsible for it.
  • Any Tech 4 abroad involves an EIP! Take advantage of the free slots you will have to advance it.
cost:
Financial Overview (4th year Epitech)

  • You must pay the tuition fees for the 4th year of EPITECH, as well as the re-registration fees and related fees.
  • EPITECH covers the tuition fees. Epitech covers tuition only for required credits.
  • The tuition supplement payable by you is indicated at the top of this page (if applicable).
  • Other costs at your expense include: travel, accommodation on site, insurance, and everyday expenses (books, food, transport, etc.)


Other Expenses / Estimated Budget (more information here)

The local currency is the Dollar. 1 € = 1.16USD (rate as of October 2025).

Please check the Numbeo website to compare the cost of living between your city of origin and your city of exchange. Please note that everyone's budget will be different according to one's lifestyle.


Keep in mind that life in Southern California is generally more expensive than in other parts of the US.


  • Round trip flights: about 1000€, depending on the airline & travel dates
  • Health insurance: ~$950 / quarter
  • Visa application fees: ~500€
  • Books ~500$
  • Rent/housing and utilities ~3750$ / quarter
  • Food ~1000$ / quarter
  • Transportation = unlimited local bus included in student services fees
  • Phone / internat ~180$


These prices are indicative and may change.
